title: Ad Click Aggregator
summary: Count billions of ad clicks per day for billing and dashboards: fast redirect, an append-only click stream, windowed aggregation with exactly-once semantics, dedup and fraud filtering, and an OLAP store for queries.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Users click an ad and are redirected to the advertiser's site
Advertisers query click counts per ad over time (minute granularity), filtered by dimensions
Counts must be accurate — they drive billing
Queries over recent data within ~1 minute of the click; sub-second dashboard queries

blocks.text: Write volume is high, query patterns are known in advance (ad × minute × dimensions) — pre-aggregate.

blocks.caption: Lambda-ish: fast stream path + batch reconciliation

items: Key the stream by ad_id; 1-minute **tumbling windows** on **event time**, not processing time.
**Watermarks** decide when a window is complete; allow a small lateness and route very late events to a side output reconciled by the batch job.
**Exactly-once:** Flink checkpoints state and offsets together and writes results with a two-phase-commit or idempotent upsert keyed by (ad_id, minute).
Hot ads: pre-aggregate per partition then combine, or salt the key (ad_id#n) and merge.

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: Because results are keyed by (ad_id, window_start), the sink write is an idempotent upsert — replays after a failure overwrite instead of double counting.

items: Each impression gets a signed impression id; the click carries it. Dedup clicks on (impression_id) within a window using keyed state with TTL.
Bot filtering: IP / user-agent heuristics, click rate per user, ML scoring — flag rather than drop so billing can be adjusted.
Approximate unique users per ad: HyperLogLog sketches merged across windows.
Click service is stateless; it writes to Kafka (acks=all) before redirecting — or redirects immediately and logs async if latency matters more.
Kafka partitions by ad_id; enough partitions for peak throughput.
OLAP store with rollups by minute → hour → day; keep raw data in the lake for audits and recompute.
Batch reconciliation compares stream totals with the raw lake and corrects the serving table.

cols.title: Stream only (Kappa)
cons: Replays of long history are slow; needs long retention

cols.title: Stream + batch (Lambda)
pros: Batch gives an authoritative billing number
cons: Two code paths to keep in sync

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Aggregate on event time in one-minute windows, keyed by ad, with idempotent upserts — and keep the raw log so billing can always be recomputed.

items.title: HLD
items.text: Click service → Kafka → Flink → OLAP; raw lake.

items.q: How would you compute top-100 ads in the last hour?
items.a: Per-minute counts per ad → sliding 60-minute sum → per-partition top-K heaps merged; or Count-Min sketch + heap for approximate.

items.q: Why not increment a counter in Redis per click?
items.a: Works for small scale, but gives no event-time windows, no replay, and a lost Redis node loses counts.

items.q: How do you query arbitrary dimensions?
items.a: Store per-minute aggregates with dimension columns in a columnar OLAP store; it scans/filters quickly.

items: Exactly-once = checkpoints + idempotent upsert by (ad, minute).
Dedup by impression id; HLL for uniques.
Raw lake + batch recompute for billing.
